topic: You are looking at the past
hook: The Sun you see is 8 minutes old.
claim: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth, so we see the Sun (and every star) as it was when the light left it.
why_now: Light-travel-time Short at 300x breakout, 1.8M views this month
visuals: NASA SDO Sun footage, Hubble deep field, ISS sunrise

topic: Why you can't nuke a hurricane
hook: A hurricane releases more energy than a nuke. Constantly.
claim: A mature hurricane's heat release is like a 10-megaton bomb going off every 20 minutes, so a nuclear blast would not stop it and would spread fallout (NOAA HRD FAQ).
why_now: 'What if we nuked a hurricane' Short at 23x and 1.3K VPH; rising keyword 'disasters explained' +232%; Typhoon Arnab in NASA EO
visuals: NASA ISS and GOES hurricane footage, eye-of-storm flyovers

hook: Space is full of sunlight. So why is it black?
claim: Our sky looks blue because air molecules scatter blue sunlight toward our eyes; in space there is almost no air to scatter light, so the sky looks black even in full sunlight.
why_now: 'Why is space pitch black?' Short at 41x this week; 'real color of space' cluster breaking out
visuals: NASA spacewalk footage against black sky, ISS view of Earth's blue limb

hook: The Sun isn't yellow. It's white.
claim: The Sun emits all visible colors, which combine to white; it looks yellow from the ground because the atmosphere scatters away some blue light.
why_now: TikTok on the Sun's real color: 1M views at 34.9x this month
visuals: ISS photos of the Sun from orbit, NASA SDO, sunset from ISS

hook: Auroras are the Sun hitting our air.
claim: Charged particles from the Sun, steered by Earth's magnetic field, collide with oxygen and nitrogen high in the atmosphere, which then glow green, red, and purple.
why_now: Solar Cycle 25 peak; G2 storm watch Oct 8-9 put aurora in reach of up to 22 US states
visuals: NASA ISS aurora time-lapses, SDO solar flare footage

hook: The Moon is leaving us. Slowly.
claim: The Moon moves about 3.8 cm farther from Earth each year because of tidal interactions.
why_now: 'What if' niche surging (ifverse +52,580%); 'what would happen if the moon crashed into earth?' +725%
visuals: NASA LRO Moon footage, Apollo laser retroreflector photos, Earthrise

topic: Why stars twinkle but planets don't
hook: Stars twinkle. Planets don't. Here's why.
claim: Stars are so far away they are point sources, so turbulent air bends their light around and they flicker; planets show a tiny disk whose many points average out.
why_now: IG Reel on this exact question: 843.5K views at 35.8x this month
visuals: NASA night-sky footage, ISS photos of atmosphere layer, planets (Jupiter, Venus) imagery

hook: One teaspoon of this weighs a billion tons.
claim: Neutron stars pack more than the Sun's mass into a city-sized ball, so a sugar-cube-sized piece would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
why_now: Pulsar-density Reel: 770K views at 144x this month
visuals: NASA Goddard SVS pulsar and neutron-star animations, Crab Nebula (Hubble/Chandra)

hook: Frozen ground holds more carbon than the sky.
claim: Permafrost soils hold roughly twice as much carbon as is currently in the atmosphere; thawing lets microbes release it as CO2 and methane.
visuals: NASA ABoVE Arctic footage, Landsat thaw-lake imagery, Earth Observatory Arctic images
